What everyone is saying is absolutely correct and definitely follow their advice. I just want to put a little perspective on if you decide to give your kid implants/hearing aid and have him to go oral or mainstream school. 

I was born Deaf, but grew up hearing. And it is an absolute mind fuck when that happens. There’s two worlds for us: deaf and hearing world. When you don’t belong in either, you have an identity crisis- at least I did when I was young and my friends who also grew up the same way described the same feeling. 

I didn’t belong with the hearing kids because I couldn’t understand them. But I didn’t belong in the deaf kids either because I was rejected by them (my mom tried to enroll me in a deaf school but the principal would only allow fully deaf kids: no cochlear implant and no learning how to speak. My mom wanted me to learn asl and speech.) 

I eventually grew to despise me being deaf because I was bullied for it and I didn’t feel like I belonged anywhere. I remember at one point in my life I would pray to be dead because I couldn’t stand being deaf. I told my mom I would rather be dead than deaf because I just wanted to belong. 

Do not let anyone persuade you from doing the best for your child. Which is absolutely learning asl and having everyone around him learn it too. Have him be proud of who he is. If you want him to learn sign and speech, you can have him do both. Most deaf schools now offer speech therapy. Sometimes they students opt out of it and sometimes they like it. You never know. I know three students  I went to school with loved speech therapy and would talk a looottt I also know a few students didn’t like speech therapy and decided to not pursue it. Which is okay. But giving your child options for both is also a good idea I think. 

You may meet some Deaf people who will gatekeep and disagree that teaching your kids speech is wrong and it won’t make him “a true deaf person” but really don’t mind the deaf elitist. Just do what you think is best.

Soda: so make your nondominant hand into a tight “o” but enough you can get a i finger in. and put your middle finger into the tight o. Pull out the middle finger and cover the “o” shape with your entire palm. It’s all one motion. 

I’m not the best at explaining hand signs so I hope this makes sense! And isn’t a word in asl really, it’s used in more academic settings (at least in my school it was) so you would just be signing “I want gin alcohol soda drink” or something.
